ClaimCheck.description:
The questions behind a score: what was asked, answered, or skipped.

Two numbers are not provenance. A score that carries a claim check says
which questions produced it — ``asked`` — and what came back: the
``answers`` the person gave and the ``skips`` with a recorded reason.

``verified`` is derived, never typed in: a check is verified when at least
one question was answered by the person. A check of only skips is
unverified, so an outcome built on an assumption says so instead of
borrowing the confidence of a number.

answers.description: The answers the person gave, in order
answers.title: Answers

asked.description: The questions put to the person
asked.title: Asked

skips.description: Questions skipped, each with a reason
skips.title: Skips

ClaimCheck.title: ClaimCheck

ClaimSkip.description:
One question that went unanswered, and why it was skipped.

A skip without a reason is not a skip, it is a missing answer, so
``reason`` is required and must not be blank.

question.description: The question that was not answered
question.title: Question

reason.description: Why it was skipped; never blank
reason.title: Reason

get.description:
Return an outcome's accepted score snapshots, oldest first.

Snapshots carry the score and its sample/method companions. The signed delta
is served separately at ``/outcomes/{id}/delta`` so this list shape stays
identical across the local and MCP backends.

get.description:
Return the paired survey inputs a stored band was reproduced from (B3.1).

``inputs: null`` means no input set is retained — a legacy or aggregate-only
outcome — which is a distinct state from a retained set and never an empty
list that would read as zero responses. Each input carries only an opaque
per-pair token and the two numbers, so the read shape is de-identified.

schema.title: Response Get Outcome Inputs Api Outcomes  Outcome Id  Inputs Get

get.description:
Return an outcome's stored band and its provenance (B3.2).

``band: null`` means the score carries no band at all — an estimate or an
unscored outcome — which is a distinct state from a zero-width band. A
stored band reports the sample, seed, confidence level, method and
computed-at it was recorded with, plus whether a later snapshot moved the
score it came from, so a consumer never presents a stale band as current.
